questions.q: Several analytics teams must share curated datasets inside one company. Producers want consumers to request access, an approver to accept, and access to follow the consumer team rather than individual users. Which design fits?

options.t: Publish assets in SageMaker Catalog and let consumer projects subscribe
options.why: Right: access is requested, approved and fulfilled per project.

options.t: Grant each analyst an IAM user policy on the S3 bucket
options.why: Wrong: per-user grants have no approval flow and do not follow the team.

options.t: Copy the datasets into every team's account
options.why: Wrong: copies add cost and drift, and have no approval workflow.

options.t: Publish the data as AWS Data Exchange products
options.why: Wrong: Data Exchange targets external data sharing, not internal governed sharing.

questions.explain: Internal governed sharing with approval is publish/subscribe in SageMaker Catalog.
questions.remember: Governed internal sharing with approval, per project → SageMaker Catalog publish/subscribe.
variants: Sharing with external vendors or customers → AWS Data Exchange.
Only table/column permissions in a lake, no catalog needed → Lake Formation alone.

questions.q: An administrator wants every new project in a domain to start with the same set of blueprints, with some tools available later on demand. Which feature defines this?

options.t: IAM permissions boundary
options.why: Wrong: it limits permissions but does not define what a project gets.

options.t: A project profile
options.why: Right: a collection of blueprints, each enabled at creation or available on demand.

options.t: A business glossary
options.why: Wrong: glossary terms describe data, not project resources.

options.t: A data source
options.why: Wrong: a data source imports metadata, it does not provision project tools.

questions.explain: Project profiles are templates made of blueprints.
questions.remember: What a project gets at creation or on demand → project profile (a set of blueprints); only domain administrators manage profiles.
variants: Template types: All capabilities, SQL analytics, Generative AI application development, Custom.
Who can create profiles → domain administrators only.

questions.q: A new analyst joins a team that already has access to governed data in a SageMaker Unified Studio project. What is the most scalable way to give access?

options.t: Add a bucket policy for the analyst's IAM user
options.why: Wrong: bypasses the project and does not scale.

options.t: Create a new domain for the analyst
options.why: Wrong: a domain is the top-level boundary, far too heavy.

options.t: Share the project role credentials
options.why: Wrong: sharing credentials breaks least privilege and auditing.

options.t: Add the analyst to the Identity Center group mapped to the project
options.why: Right: data access flows through the project role, so membership gives access.

questions.explain: Project membership drives access; groups scale it.
questions.remember: Data access goes through the project role, so manage membership (via Identity Center groups), not per-user data grants.
variants: Revoke access → remove membership; data permissions stay untouched.
User cannot sign in at all → not assigned to the domain or an Identity Center/SAML mismatch.

questions.q: Consumers of a published table must see only some columns and rows. Which layer enforces this?

options.t: The business glossary
options.why: Wrong: glossary terms are metadata and enforce nothing.

options.t: Lake Formation filters on the published asset
options.why: Right: Lake Formation enforces column, row and cell permissions.

options.t: Lineage graphs
options.why: Wrong: lineage traces data movement and does not restrict access.

options.t: Metadata forms
options.why: Wrong: they hold fields such as owner or classification, not permissions.

questions.explain: Fine-grained enforcement comes from Lake Formation.
questions.remember: Fine-grained (column/row/cell) access on catalog data → Lake Formation filters; the Catalog adds the business layer.
variants: Need to trace where data came from → lineage.

questions.q: A team already has technical metadata in the Glue Data Catalog and wants owners, descriptions and business terms added so people can search by business meaning. What should they do?

options.t: Replace the Glue Data Catalog with Lake Formation
options.why: Wrong: Lake Formation manages permissions, not business metadata.

options.t: Use Glue as a source and enrich the assets in SageMaker Catalog
options.why: Right: the Catalog layers business metadata on top of Glue.

options.t: Store descriptions in S3 object tags
options.why: Wrong: not searchable as a business catalog.

options.t: Rebuild all tables in Redshift
options.why: Wrong: unnecessary migration.

questions.explain: Glue holds technical metadata; the Catalog adds the business layer.
questions.remember: Business context on lake tables → Glue Data Catalog as source plus SageMaker Catalog enrichment (glossary, metadata forms).
variants: Only technical metadata needed → Glue Data Catalog alone.
Metadata is stale → schedule data source runs, since metadata is imported, not live.

questions.q: A subscription was approved, but the consumer's Athena query fails with access errors. Which are likely causes?  Choose 2.

options.t: The consumer project has too few members
options.why: Wrong: membership count does not affect data access.

options.t: The S3 location is not registered with Lake Formation, or grants are missing
options.why: Right: Lake Formation must hold the grants and the registered location.

options.t: The glossary has no terms
options.why: Wrong: the glossary does not gate queries.

options.t: The KMS key policy does not let the project role decrypt
options.why: Right: the project role needs kms:Decrypt on keys protecting the data.

questions.explain: Check Lake Formation grants/registration and KMS key access.
questions.remember: Approved subscription but query fails → Lake Formation grants or registration, or KMS permissions for the project role.
variants: Asset missing from inventory → data source run failed or lacks permissions.
Cannot create project → blueprint not enabled, account not associated, role or quota issue.

questions.q: An auditor asks where a dataset's data came from and how it was transformed. Which capability answers this in SageMaker Catalog?

options.t: Subscription approvals
options.why: Wrong: they show who got access, not data origin.

options.t: Project profiles
options.why: Wrong: they define project templates.

options.t: Lineage
options.why: Right: lineage tracks data movement and transformation.

options.t: Data source schedules
options.why: Wrong: they control metadata import timing.

questions.explain: Lineage stores the graph of origin and transformation.
questions.remember: Trace data origin and transformations → lineage in the Catalog.
variants: Lineage missing → the job does not emit lineage events or integration is not enabled.
Who accessed data → CloudTrail, subscription history and Lake Formation logs.

questions.q: Costs in SageMaker Unified Studio projects are rising. Which levers reduce spend?  Choose 2.

options.t: Share data through subscriptions or datashares instead of copies
options.why: Right: avoids duplicate storage.

options.t: Allow every compute type in every profile
options.why: Wrong: this raises cost; limiting compute in project profiles lowers it.

options.t: Restrict compute choices in project profiles
options.why: Right: profiles define which tools projects can use.

options.t: Run data source imports every minute
options.why: Wrong: frequent runs add compute cost; schedule them sparingly.

questions.explain: Cost comes from underlying services; constrain profiles and avoid copies.
questions.remember: You pay for the underlying services, so limit compute in project profiles, auto-stop idle resources, budget per project, and share rather than copy.
variants: Idle notebook spaces or clusters → auto-stop.
Track spend per team → tag project resources and set budgets per project.
